literal.prompt: Как называется место, где соседние кости или кость и хрящ образуют соединение?

literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax 9.1 L30 defines a joint as the place where adjacent bones, or bone and cartilage, come together to form a connection. The prompt paraphrases that definition; “Сустав” alone names the place. “Сухожилие” and “Мышца” are related musculoskeletal structures (OpenStax 11.1 L30), while “Хрящ” is the material at a cartilaginous joint (OpenStax 9.1 L35), so the alternatives are related but do not name the place.

literalGroups.literal: Сустав — место, где соседние кости или кость и хрящ образуют соединение. По степени подвижности суставы бывают неподвижными, малоподвижными или свободно подвижными.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax 9.1 L30 directly defines a joint as a connection place involving adjacent bones or bone and cartilage. L37-L38 classify joints by movement as immobile, slightly movable, or freely movable, supporting the second sentence.

literalGroups.literal: По степени подвижности суставы делят на неподвижные, малоподвижные и свободно подвижные.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note adds the three functional mobility classes of joints; OpenStax 9.1 L37-L38 names synarthrosis, amphiarthrosis, and diarthrosis and defines their movement ranges.

literalGroups.literal: Сухожилие — прочная полоса соединительной ткани, которая соединяет мышцу с костью.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax 11.1 L30 describes tendons as strong bands of dense, regular connective tissue that connect muscles to bones.

literalGroups.literal: Сокращение мышечных волокон создаёт натяжение, которое передаётся сухожилиям для движения скелета.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax 11.1 L30 states that skeletal-muscle fiber contraction creates tension transferred to tendons to move the skeleton.

literalGroups.literal: В хрящевом суставе соседние кости соединены гиалиновым или волокнистым хрящом.
literalGroups.primaryGround: OpenStax 9.1 L35 states that at a cartilaginous joint the bones are joined by hyaline cartilage or fibrocartilage.

absoluteDifficulty.assessment: A broad adult audience commonly recognizes a joint as the place where body parts meet. The prompt states the defining relation directly, and the options are short, familiar musculoskeletal structures or tissue; no specialized terminology or multistep reasoning is needed. The new place-focused wording separates the answer from tendon and ligament functions.
